root_cause: BROWSER_STEP_COMPLETED only published a REQUEST_PROGRESS event consumed solely by tutorial_integration; the only calls into the partial-submission callback came from a dead BROWSER_RESULT_PARTIAL event type and a post-completion chunk-split of the already-final description, so step content never reached the sentence/TTS queue during task execution.

browser_automation: check current page before treating a named section as a search query elsewhere
root_cause: Live repro: 'click on Premium summer picks section' (a context-free follow-up task) reached a fresh browser-use agent with no memory of the prior turn that had already found this section on the Amazon homepage. The agent's system prompt had no instruction to check the current page before treating a named section as a search query, so it typed the name into Amazon's search bar and searched the whole site instead of scrolling the current page, eventually reporting the section as unavailable even though it was visible seconds earlier.
solution: Added a CHECK THE CURRENT PAGE BEFORE SEARCHING ELSEWHERE section to _build_agent_system_message() (client/modules/browser_automation/browser_llm.py) -- before using site search or navigating away, the agent must first scroll the current page to check if the named item/section is already visible there. Fixed in the browser agent's own prompt, not the server-side SKILL.md routing prompt (user correction: the routing task was fine, the failure was the agent not checking the current page).

description: orchestrator: wire up dead active-browser followup guard in arun_streaming
root_cause: _force_browser_followup_action() was added in v5.0.0.845/846 to convert an action:null answer into a fresh browser_use call while a browser session is active, but was never actually called anywhere -- not in run() (which computes browser_followup_task but never applies it) and not in arun_streaming() (the real production path), which also never computed browser_followup_task at all. Live repro: with Amazon open, 'Go to best seller' fell through to the generic canned reply 'I'm here. How can I help?' instead of navigating.
solution: Added browser_followup_task computation + _force_browser_followup_action() call on iteration 1 to both run() and arun_streaming(); in arun_streaming(), also suppress live sentence-streaming of the action:null text whenever the force is about to override it, since the streaming loop yields sentences token-by-token before the full response is parsed -- without suppression the wrong text would already be spoken before the override took effect.

description: browser_use: restore target_tab field for switch-tab/new-tab requests
root_cause: v5.0.0.847 dropped target_tab/tab_intent/tab_reason from the browser_use LLM contract assuming they were unused; browser_request_orchestration.py's _resolve_request_target_tab() still defaults to current when absent, which both instructs the agent to stay on the current tab and keeps _enforce_owned_content_tab()'s step-callback guard active, forcibly refocusing back to the original tab after every step -- confirmed by user as a regression, working before v5.0.0.847.
solution: Restored target_tab (current|existing|new) to the browser_use SKILL.md contract -- existing for Switch to a tab, new for Open a new blank tab, omitted elsewhere; updated test_browser_skill_prompt.py to match.

description: browser_automation: document extract content taxonomy, extend item metadata to product/article fields
root_cause: User wanted prices/rating/review-purchase counts covered for shopping-style sites too, and asked to fix scope once via a documented content-type taxonomy rather than re-deriving it ad hoc for each new content type.
solution: Documented an Extract Content Taxonomy table in flows/browser.md (video/product/article/fallback -> required fields), renamed VIDEO METADATA to ITEM METADATA in _build_agent_system_message() and the forced extract() query to cover all four types, keeping both in sync with the documented table.

description: browser_automation: include channel name and view count for YouTube/similar video items in extract-based descriptions
root_cause: The pre-simplification browser_use/SKILL.md explicitly asked for title, views, channel, and duration on video results; the v5.0.0.847 skill-contract simplification dropped that per-item detail, leaving only bare titles in both the agent system prompt and the forced-rewrite extract query.
solution: Added VIDEO METADATA guidance to _build_agent_system_message() (browser_llm.py) and extended the forced extract() query in _force_grounded_final_answer() (browser_session_lifecycle.py) to require channel name and view count for YouTube/similar video items.

description: browser_automation: add READ-ONLY TASK RESTRICTION to browser-use agent system prompt
root_cause: _build_agent_system_message() only advised trying extract first for read-only tasks (FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING), never hard-forbidding click/type/submit/play/navigate, so the browser-use agent could still interact with the page (e.g. click a video thumbnail) on a plain read/describe request, sometimes starting media playback.
solution: Added a READ-ONLY TASK RESTRICTION section to _build_agent_system_message() in client/modules/browser_automation/browser_llm.py: for tasks that only ask to read/check/find out/describe, the agent must not click/type/submit/play/pause/navigate — only scroll and extract are allowed.

root_cause: BOOTSTRAP rules 8b/8c already make the model reason through common/not_common and specific/no_specific internally as part of its single JSON response, but that verdict was never captured as an explicit field; active_skill was tracked in session_registry but never assembled into a debug data point alongside it.

browser_use: scroll default bounded amount via pages parameter
root_cause: TASK COMPLETION DISCIPLINE (browser_llm.py:747-763) required exact counts for repeatable actions but never defined a default for a count-less scroll, nor bounded open-ended 'to the end' requests; ScrollAction.pages (browser_use/tools/views.py:79-82) was the unused real lever for scroll amount.
solution: Extended TASK COMPLETION DISCIPLINE with a SCROLL AMOUNT sub-rule: no count -> one call pages=1.0; explicit count N -> one call pages=N; 'to the end/bottom/top' -> one bounded call pages~=10, using the library's own parameter instead of chaining repeated scroll calls.

description: browser_use: FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING requires naming specific list items
root_cause: FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING (v5.0.0.823) required 'some real fact' after extract but never distinguished list content from generic page structure; live test showed the model satisfied the rule with nav-menu/search-bar description instead of naming actual video titles.
solution: Added explicit sub-rule inside FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING: if extracted content includes a list of similar items (videos, products, search results, articles), the agent MUST name the specific items found — generic page structure alone is not acceptable while a list is present.

description: browser_use: code-enforce FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING with one corrective extract retry
root_cause: FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING (browser_llm.py, v5.0.0.821/822) is a prompt-only instruction; browser-use's own use_judge/_judge_and_log only logs a verdict after done is already accepted, never blocks/retries; live test confirmed the model calls done with zero extract calls in its trajectory despite the unconditional instruction.
solution: _run_agent() (browser_session_lifecycle.py) now verifies compliance: done_callback stores history instead of queuing BROWSER_TASK_COMPLETED directly; after agent.run() returns, _history_used_extract(history) checks action_names() for extract; if missing, exactly one corrective agent.add_new_task()+agent.run(max_steps=3) retry runs before the task is accepted as complete.

description: browser_use FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING now unconditional, no action-only exemption
root_cause: browser_llm.py:774-786 _build_agent_system_message() FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING (v5.0.0.821) still gated extract-before-done on the final answer needing to state a fact, plus an explicit action-only exemption sentence — plain action tasks (open X, click X, go back) could skip extract entirely.
solution: Rewrote the section to be unconditional: 'Reaching a page is NEVER sufficient to call done on its own, for any task' — extract-before-done now applies to every browser_use task including action-only ones, no exemption clause remains.

description: browser_use final answer grounding generalized beyond list tasks
root_cause: browser_llm.py:774-784 _build_agent_system_message() — extract-before-done requirement (LIST/ENUMERATION TASKS) was scoped only to list/enumeration tasks; other content-fact final answers (e.g. plain navigation/description requests) could call done without extract, producing an ungrounded answer. Live repro via experiments/browser_use_check, session 1bab5adf, 2026-07-03.
solution: Generalized LIST/ENUMERATION TASKS to FACTUAL ANSWER GROUNDING in browser_llm.py:_build_agent_system_message() — extract-before-done now required whenever the final answer must state any page-content fact, not just for lists; pure action-only tasks remain exempt.
